subject: Scanone: some markers change names, need to retain original marker names

messages.author: df8b0e8623cf4342
messages.subject: Scanone: some markers change names, need to retain original marker names
parts:
Hi,

I need to save the LOD scores for all the markers in my map, which I have done using scanone. In the output, some marker names are changed from their original number to something like "c1.loc2", but I need to retain the original marker names for future use. Why does Rqtl do this and how can I fix it?

This is my script:
info<-(scanone(trait))
traitinfo<-data.frame(info)
write.csv(traitinfo, file="Anthocyanininfo.csv")


This is the output I get in my .csv file:
chr pos lod
67679 1 1.702 0.748070691
67685 1 1.702 0.748070692
c1.loc1 1 1.758 0.753997426
c1.loc2 1 2.758 0.860399792
56068 1 3.403 0.926782219


Thanks!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Scanone: some markers change names, need to retain original marker names
parts:
scanone performs calculations at the markers plus at positions between markers ("pseudomarkers") at a density defined by the step argument in calc.genoprob (or, for method="imp", sim.geno).

You could rerun calc.genoprob with step=0, and then rerun scanone, and the results will not include any such pseudomarkers.

Or you could remove them afterwards by subsetting with your marker names, or search for the pattern c[chr].loc[pos]. Here's an example.

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1)
out <- scanone(hyper)

# use marker names
out_onlymarkers_1 <- out[markernames(hyper),]

# search for pseudomarkers to remove
out_onlymarkers_2 <- out[!grepl("^c.+\\.loc-*[0-9]+", rownames(out)), ]

karl
